g01.def: Spreading the cost of a more expensive asset over several years instead of booking it all at purchase.

g02.def: A summary of what the company owns (assets) and owes (liabilities and equity) at a given point in time.

g03.def: The shared Swedish standard for how bookkeeping accounts are numbered and grouped. Bokix uses BAS 2025 by default.

g04.def: Closing the financial year, when the income statement and balance sheet are put together for the whole year.

g05.def: The two sides of bookkeeping. You do not need to know them: choose Simple when you book, pick what happened, and Bokix does the rest. Every voucher has the same amount on both sides.

g06.def: A business form without its own legal personality. You and the business are the same taxpayer.

g07.def: The registration showing that the company itself is responsible for paying its tax and contributions.

g08.def: The VAT you pay on what you buy for the company. It can usually be deducted from output VAT.

g09.def: The list of all accounts a company books its transactions against.

g10.def: An annual report to the Swedish Tax Agency, for example about salary paid to employees.

g11.def: The invoice you send to a customer for goods or services sold.

g12.def: The invoice you receive and have to pay for something you bought.

g13.def: The periodic report to the Swedish Tax Agency showing output VAT minus input VAT. The difference is paid in or refunded.

g14.def: The twelve-month period that the bookkeeping and year-end closing follow. For most, the same as the calendar year.

g15.def: A summary of income minus costs over a period, showing whether the result was a profit or a loss.

g16.def: The VAT you charge customers when you sell. It is paid to the Swedish Tax Agency, less input VAT.

g17.def: The booked record of a transaction: date, amount and which accounts are affected.

g18.def: The formal document that summarises the year-end closing and (for limited companies, among others) is filed with the Swedish Companies Registration Office.
